segments.title: Chương 160: 0160 【Anh Trần Nâng Cấp Xe】
segments.content:
Chapter 163: 0160 CEO Chen's Ride Upgrade

Perhaps due to superstition, none of the companies moving into the building rented space on the 14th floor when other floors were available.

Chen Guiliang couldn't be bothered with such things. Since he could take his pick of the offices on the 14th floor, of course he was going to move the company there.

He rented the entire floor!

The day after the financing agreement was signed, the renovation crew entered the site.

At the same time, the recruitment process also began.

Chen Guiliang served as CEO, concurrently managing CPO tasks like product planning.

Guo Feng served as CTO.

Ao Yanchen served as COO.

Chang Zhongxiang, the finance professional recommended by the investors, served as CFO.

Xie Yang served as CMO, also managing some CPO duties.

The first day of recruitment was mainly for HR, finance, legal, and administrative staff.

The group sat in a row, with Chen Guiliang in the very center. "Please introduce yourself."

"My name is Wei Xiaokang, a recent graduate from Beiyou's Information Engineering program. During my time at university, I was a long-term moderator for the job-seeking and career-life forums on Beiyou's two major BBSes."

A rather handsome young man, though still a bit green, spoke with great confidence. "Although I have no formal work experience, I am very familiar with HR. I know which companies the Beiyou graduates from the past two years have gone to, and I also know about their situations at those companies. I understand the psychological state of employees…"

Ao Yanchen asked, "Have you interned anywhere?"

"I interned in the sales and product departments at Datang Telecom," Wei Xiaokang replied.

Chen Guiliang asked, "What are your thoughts on Datang Telecom? You don't have to answer if it involves ethical or confidentiality issues."

Wei Xiaokang said, "Datang's TDSCDMA technology has a low level of maturity, and its commercialization is severely lagging. It's still in the trial network phase, which makes the company's revenue heavily reliant on its traditional business. It's too dependent on policy support."

"I was asking about Datang's HR department," Chen Guiliang said with a smile.

Wei Xiaokang replied, "It has many strengths. After all, it's a state-owned enterprise, and it can leverage policies to attract high-end talent. But its incentive mechanisms are rigid, its salary structure is monotonous, promotion channels are narrow, seniority is a major factor, performance reviews are a formality, there's no exit mechanism, the hiring process is lengthy, and training is disconnected from practice…"

My goodness, he rattled off a whole bunch of Datang Telecom's shortcomings in one breath.

Ao Yanchen asked, "If you were the head of Datang Telecom's HR department, how do you think you should reform those shortcomings?"

"It's impossible to reform, because it's a state-owned enterprise," Wei Xiaokang added, "at the very least, the head of the HR department couldn't initiate it. It would require a decisive CEO of Datang Telecom."

Chen Guiliang asked, "What kind of HR management system do you think ByteDance should implement?"

Wei Xiaokang said, "That depends on ByteDance's corporate culture and business philosophy. On the career-life forums of Beiyou's two major platforms, I've spoken with senior schoolmates from different companies. Those companies' HR systems all vary; they're each formulated according to their own circumstances. The kind of boss and upper management you have determines the kind of HR system you'll have."

"What are your salary expectations?"

"I'm fine with whatever you see fit. I just graduated this year, so I'm more focused on being able to grow together with ByteDance."

"Alright, you can go home and wait for our decision," Chen Guiliang said.

Wei Xiaokang stood up, bowed, and left the interview site full of anticipation.

"Please introduce yourself."

"My name is Shi Qian, a graduate of Peking University's law school. Four years ago, I joined King & Wood Mallesons, one of China's largest and most international law firms, which specializes in capital markets, cross-border M&A, intellectual property, and so on. I was a paralegal for only half a year before being promoted to junior associate, and two and a half years later, I was promoted to mid-level associate. I am well-versed in laws related to intellectual property and capital markets. You can read the details of the major cases I've handled, esteemed interviewers…"

"Why didn't you stay at King & Wood?"

"Because I saw an opportunity at ByteDance."

"What are your requirements for the position and salary?"

"Your company has just received venture capital. Even with expansion, you won't have many legal staff. I propose that a single legal specialist position would be sufficient. I would like to take on that role, for a monthly salary of ten thousand."

"That salary seems far below what a mid-level associate at King & Wood earns."

"I am optimistic about your company's growth. After one year, I hope to have my salary adjusted, and I'll want an annual salary by then. Therefore, I will only sign a one-year employment contract. If I don't perform well, you can dismiss me when the contract expires. If the annual salary you offer isn't enough, I will also choose to leave."

The golden reputation of a 19-year-old billionaire was more effective than any advertisement, attracting a large number of high-quality talents to submit their resumes.

Similarly, the number of users on Xiaonei Wang was also surging.

Many university students who hadn't been interested in Xiaonei Wang flocked to register after seeing the news. Because Chen Guiliang was their peer, they felt a natural sense of affinity.

Due to the rapid increase in university student users, Xiaonei Wang had to delay its launch date for middle school students.

Guo Feng proposed building their own server room. Compared to renting servers, it would be more secure and, in the long run, more cost-effective.

But this was a rather troublesome matter, and for now, they didn't have the energy for it.

"You guys handle things this afternoon, I have to take my final exams," Chen Guiliang left around noon.

Ao Yanchen said, "I have an exam tomorrow morning, too."

Guo Feng said, "Mine's tomorrow afternoon."

Chang Zhongxiang, the finance professional recommended by the investors, felt a mix of helplessness and amusement upon hearing their conversation.

Another applicant came in, crossing paths with Chen Guiliang on his way out.

Once outside, the waiting interviewees recognized him and greeted him one after another, "Hello, CEO Chen!"

All of these people were under thirty years old.

There were even recent graduates who had been hired by major tech companies but were now trying their luck at ByteDance, hoping for a better opportunity. After all, competition at the big companies was fierce, while it was easier to be valued at a startup.

"Everyone, go down to the first floor for lunch, we'll continue in the afternoon," Chen Guiliang said. "The company will settle the bill with the cafeteria for the interviewees' lunches."

Seeing that Chen Guiliang was also heading downstairs, everyone followed him, packing the elevator to the brim.

"CEO Chen, are you really just 19 years old?"

"Yeah, my birthday is two days before the Gaokao every year."

"That's amazing!"

"CEO Chen, I graduated from Renmin University. I was originally planning to stay at the university and go into politics, but after seeing your story in the news, I was inspired and came here specifically to apply."

"I hope your interview is successful."

"CEO Chen…"

The afternoon exams were Modern History and Thought and Morality. Chen Guiliang felt he could muddle through them.

He knew the basic content, and though he couldn't remember some of the details, he could piece together enough to answer the questions. As long as the professor wasn't too strict, passing shouldn't be a problem.

The evening exam was Critical Writing and Academic Norms, which was even less of a problem. A few hours of reviewing the key points would be enough to pass.

During the exam, classmates kept looking at him.

Even the proctoring teacher walked over to Chen Guiliang's side and stood there, watching him answer the questions, as if his exam paper was more pleasing to the eye than the others'.

It wasn't uncommon for Olympic champions and movie stars to study at Peking University.

But a 19-year-old billionaire was one of a kind!

The evening exam was a mandatory course exclusive to the Yuanpei Program, so the entire class was finally gathered together again.

Albeit in an examination hall.

As soon as Chen Guiliang walked outside the exam hall, he was surrounded by his classmates. They shouted congratulations and then unanimously demanded that he treat them.

"After all the exams are over, I'll treat the entire class, including our academic advisor, to a huge meal!" Chen Guiliang announced.

"CEO Chen is awesome!"

"Hahahaha…"

These guys were just waiting to see Chen Guiliang "go broke," as a way to soothe their envy, jealousy, and bitterness.

There were still over twenty minutes before the exam, so after teasing Chen Guiliang, everyone started chatting animatedly, since it was rare for the Yuanpei students to all be together.

"Did you guys see the newspaper? There's a student this year who took the Gaokao at age 10."

"10 years old? You've got to be kidding. Not even the junior classes are that young."

"I bet he just did it for fun. There's no way he'll get into an undergraduate program."

Chen Guiliang, however, knew that this 10-year-old kid would get into a Tier 2 university this year.

The news was a huge sensation.

And every few years, this child prodigy would make headlines again.
